My First Thrift
Believe it or not, I had never even heard of the word thrifting before it became a trend
among teenagers today. I only came to understand what made it so interesting until I
experienced it myself for the first time buying a premium jacket at a cheaper price. What I once
assumed to be nothing more than buying old and unwanted items turned out to be a completely
new experience-something unfamiliar, exciting, and unlike anything I had encountered
before.
It all started when I saw an advertisement for a new thrift shop in town and my friends
invited me to go there. At first, I was unsure whether I should go because I preferred shopping
at a regular shop where everything was new, labelled and neatly arranged. However, my friend
kept insisting that I would enjoy it, so I decided to give it a try just for the experience.
When we arrived, I was immediately surprised by the atmosphere. The place was a
spacious indoor thrift market, brightly lit and neatly arranged, with rows of stalls stretching
across the hall. It was crowded with people, especially teenagers, all browsing through racks
of clothes, baskets of shoes, and tables filled with accessories. Soft background music played
while sellers called out friendly promotions, adding to the lively mood. It did not feel old or
dull at all. Instead, it felt vibrant, energetic, and almost like a treasure hunt where everyone
was searching excitedly for something unique and valuable.
As I walked around, I did not know where to start. There were so many items
everywhere, and at first, I felt a little overwhelmed. My friend, however, was very experienced
and started showing me how to look through items properly. She taught me to check the quality
of fabrics, inspect for hidden defects, and carefully go through each rack instead of rushing.

She also explained that thrifting requires patience, as the best finds are often hidden among
plain-looking items that others may easily overlook. According to her, some of the best items
are not always expensive and shown openly but are hidden among ordinary clothes, waiting to
be found by someone who searches carefully. Finding it is like hitting a jackpot.
After some time, I began to get the hang of it. I picked up a few clothes and examined
them carefully. Most of the items were simple, but I still enjoyed the process of searching. I
did not expect to find anything special that day, so I was just casually browsing through the
racks. Then, something unexpected happened. While going through a pile of jackets, I noticed
a leather jacket that looked different from the rest. It was in excellent condition and had a well-
known luxury brand label inside. At first, I thought it might be fake, but after checking carefully
and asking the shop owner, I realised it was authentic.
I was shocked when the owner told me the original price of the jacket. It was
extremely expensive, something I could never afford in a regular store. However, the thrift
price was unbelievably low compared to its original value. My hands were slightly shaking as
I held it, unable to believe my fortune. My friend was just as surprised and kept telling me how
lucky I was. Without thinking too long, I decided to buy it immediately. I felt a mix of
excitement and disbelief, as if I had just discovered a hidden treasure. That moment completely
changed my perception of thrifting. It was no longer just about second-hand items; it was about
unexpected discoveries, creativity, and giving forgotten things a new life.
As I continued browsing after that, nothing else compared to my "lucky find." I still
enjoyed looking around, but I kept thinking about the jacket and how unusual the experience
had been. By the end of the day, I had bought the jacket along with a few smaller items. More
importantly, I left the thrift market with a memorable experience that I would never forget. It
was exciting, surprising, and unlike any shopping trip I had ever been on.
My first thrifting experience completely changed my perception. What I thought
would be an ordinary outing turned into an unforgettable experience, especially because of the
rare item I discovered. It taught me that sometimes, the most unexpected places can lead to the

most exciting discoveries. It also made me realise that valuable things are not always found in
obvious or expensive places, but often appear when we are patient and willing to explore. From
that day on, I learned to appreciate the beauty of second-hand items and to look at things with
a more open mind.

Teen Circles, Real Issues
There are six teenagers from different backgrounds who share their experiences with
friendships and teenage relationships.
A - Ariff, 13
He takes photos of his friends, but some complain he posts too much online. He worries
they don't value his intentions. "I just want them to see how much I care," Ariff says.
B - Bella, 17
She enjoys acting, but her best friend feels jealous of her success. "I wish she could be
more positive and happy for me because sometimes I feel anxious before big
performances", Bella confesses.
C- Carol, 15
She loves cooking and sharing food with friends, but occasionally they tease her for
showing off her cooking skills. She feels torn between laughter and hurt. "Even when
they joke, I still want us to remain friends," she admits.
D - Daniel, 14
He spends weekends volunteering at an animal shelter, but his friends complain he
doesn't hang out enough. He feels guilty yet passionate about his work. "I want to help
animals and still keep my friendships strong," Daniel explains.
E -Edward, 17
He enjoys playing basketball with his team, but sometimes teammates argue about who
should lead. Edward struggles to keep the group united. "I just want us to play together
in harmony," he explains.
F - Fuzla, 16
She often feels left out when her classmates do group discussions. Reading helps her
escape, but she wishes her friends would include her more. "Sometimes I am invisible
to them," Fuzla says.
